idiom_name: typed queue facade over Node MessagePort / BullMQ
implementation_notes: TypeScript adds a compile-time message contract to the same runtime primitives JavaScript uses: a discriminated union for payloads plus a Queue<T> facade over a MessagePort pair in-process or BullMQ's Queue/Worker on Redis. The one-consumer rule is expressed in the consumer callback's type, but nothing in the type system prevents a second consumer from being attached, and broker semantics stay runtime concerns - BullMQ documents exactly-once queue semantics as a goal with at-least-once as the worst case - so the delivery discipline remains a configuration and review matter.
pitfalls: Types vanish at runtime: a worker receives unknown data, so structured clone/JSON round-trips strip classes and the union must be validated before use.
MessagePort's structured clone cannot carry functions, prototypes or DOM nodes - cross-thread models must be plain data.
At-least-once broker semantics plus unvalidated typed handlers means duplicate side effects; idempotency keys belong in the message type.
